content.overview: Section 3A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides for electronic signature. A subscriber may authenticate an electronic record by such electronic signature or electronic authentication technique which is considered reliable and may be specified in the Second Schedule. Digital signature under s. 3 is one form of electronic signature. Reliability conditions include unique linkage to the signatory, control by the signatory, detectability of alteration, and related statutory criteria.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Electronic signature or only digital signature claimed? (2) Technique reliable and/or scheduled? (3) Unique linkage and control conditions met? (4) Link to ss. 3, 5?
content.study:
s. 3A is the broader electronic-signature provision introduced by amendment. Digital signature (s. 3) remains a species of electronic signature.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Electronic signature
sections.body: Subscriber may authenticate an electronic record by electronic signature or electronic authentication technique considered reliable and as may be specified in the Second Schedule.

sections.heading: Reliability
sections.body: Technique is reliable if signature creation data are uniquely linked to and under the control of the signatory, and alterations are detectable — as the section provides.

sections.heading: Digital signature included
sections.body: Digital signature under s. 3 is a form of electronic signature under s. 3A.

sections.heading: Central specification
sections.body: Central Government may specify techniques in the Second Schedule and prescribe procedures as the Act allows.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the technique; test reliability/schedule status; relate to legal recognition under ss. 4–5.

examples.title: Scheduled technique
examples.body: Authentication using a Second Schedule electronic authentication technique that meets reliability conditions — s. 3A is satisfied subject to the official specification.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 3A replace s. 3?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 3A is broader; digital signature under s. 3 remains a recognised form of electronic signature.

distinctions.title: s. 3A electronic signature vs s. 3 digital signature
distinctions.left: Genus: electronic signature / scheduled reliable technique.
distinctions.right: Species: digital signature via asymmetric crypto and hash.

misconceptions.trap: Electronic signature and digital signature are identical.
misconceptions.correction: Digital signature is one form of electronic signature; s. 3A is the broader concept.
